{"claims":[{"claim_text":"Americans are familiar with the language of political and civil rights – one person, one voice, one vote; equal treatment before the law.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Americans are less familiar with the justification for the social rights that have been at the center of great political and social movements over the last century.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"For all citizens to flourish in a democratic society, they must be guaranteed such basic human needs as high-quality education, health care and security in old age.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"These goods are provided to every member of most democratic societies not by purchase on the private market, but through equitably financed, high-quality public goods and social insurance.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Political and civil rights cannot be exercised effectively by citizens who lack jobs, economic security, good health and the opportunity to educate themselves and their children.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Today economic inequality – the large and growing gap between high-income and wealthy households and the rest of the population – means that too many citizens are denied full participation in social and political life.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
